question.text: This Canadian province held sovereignty referendums in 1980 and 1995 because many of its residents want to become an independent country. Unlike residents in other provinces, most of its residents speak French.
question.clue: Its populace voted in 1980 and 1995 on referendums brought by its provincial "Parti", and a namesake "Bloc" represents it federally.

swap.text: The younger Trudeau replaced this Conservative as PM in 2015. He withdrew Canada from the Kyoto Protocol and slashed Canada's taxes early in his tenure to a lower corporate rate than the U.S.
swap.clue: This man led the National Citizen Coalition, a conservative lobbyist group. This former Canadian Prime Minister was succeeded by Trudeau in the late 2015 elections.

question.text: A Quebecois ["que-beck-WAA"] prime minister of Canada with this last name invoked the War Measures Act for the third time in history to end the October Crisis. His son with this surname won a third term as Canadian prime minister in 2021 federal elections.
question.answerHtml: Trudeau [accept Pierre Trudeau or Joseph Philippe Pierre Yves Elliot Trudeau or Justin Trudeau or Justin Pierre James Trudeau]
question.clue: Another politician with this name initiated the Phoenix Pay system, and was given the nickname "little potato" when attending a G20 summit in China.

swap.leadin: This modern-day province, and Quebec, made up the Province of Canada.
swap.text: Name this Canadian province which makes up modern-day Upper Canada. Ottawa and Toronto are in this province.
swap.clue: The First Nations leader Tecumseh was killed in this province during the Battle of the Thames (TIMS) in the War of 1812.

question.leadin: This man was accused of metaphorically urinating on a rug after giving a speech in Philadelphia in 1965 where he questioned U.S. foreign policy.
question.text: Name this Canadian prime minister, who earlier won a Nobel Peace Prize for negotiating an end to the Suez Crisis.
question.clue: This politician claimed "Canadians do not need to be liberated" in response to the "Vive le Quebec Libre" speech another man gave at Expo 67.

swap.leadin: This man's namesake "mania" followed his ascension to the head of the Liberal Party.
swap.text: Name this man whose government enacted a Charter of Rights and Freedoms. He proclaimed "just watch me" three days before suspending the writ of habeas corpus under the War Measures Act.
swap.clue: During an interview with Tim Ralfe, this politician defended suspending civil liberties by proclaiming "just watch me".

question.text: Both Anthony Eden and his successor Harold Macmillan were members of this British political party. Notable Hitler-appeaser Neville Chamberlain was also a member of this party.
question.clue: A foreign secretary from this party issued a statement supporting a "national home" in an Ottoman area.

swap.text: The nickname "Old Ironsides" came from now-captain Isaac Hull's victory over the Guerriere at the start of the War of 1812. The Guerriere had been heading for this British Atlantic port, now the capital of Nova Scotia.
swap.clue: During the French and Indian War, the British army kept prisoners on Georges Island in this city's harbor.

question.text: He kept appointed governor William McDougall from entering the Red River settlement and won favorable terms in the Manitoba Act. For 15 points, name this leader of the Metis who led a revolt of French-speaking Indian descendants against Canadian rule.
question.clue: This man was captured with the Cree Chief Poundmaker during the Battle of Batoche, and he appointed a tribunal which sentenced Thomas Scott to death.

swap.text: Trudeau was succeeded as prime minister by John Turner, who himself was succeeded by this Progressive Conservative. He was unsuccessful in enacting constitutional change with either the Meech Lake or Charlottetown Accords.
swap.clue: His government accepted refugees from the pro-American governments in Guatamala and El Salvador and engineered a failed agreement in Charlottetown that was to replace the Meech Lake Accord.

question.text: During his ministry, MacDonald passed the Manitoba Act and launched the Wolseley Expedition in response to this uprising of the Metis [mey-TEES] led by Louis Riel.
question.clue: The execution of Thomas Scott provoked the Wolseley Expedition, which forced one leader in this conflict to flee.

swap.leadin: At least three biographies of this man are titled Just Watch Me, referring to a famous quote.
swap.text: Name this Canadian prime minister famous for invoking the War Measures Act to crack down on dissidents during the October Crisis. He also coined the phrase "fuddle duddle" as a euphemism for "fuck off."
swap.answer: Joseph Philippe Pierre Yves Elliott Trudeau
swap.clue: This politician invoked the War Measures Act after the FLQ kidnapped Pierre LaPorte.

question.text: The Patriotes' 1837 rebellion against British rule occurred in this North American colony. This colony, which comprised present-day Quebec, was later unified with an oppositely named colony corresponding to Ontario.

swap.leadin: This man replaced Louis Saint Laurent as Prime Minister, ending 22 years of Liberal rule.
swap.text: Name this Canadian prime minister who passed the Canadian Bill of Rights in 1960. He cancelled the Avro Arrow project after agreeing to accept Bomarc nuclear missiles from the United States.
swap.clue: He also cancelled the Avro Arrow program, halting production of fighter jets in his country, when he signed NORAD with the US. Raised in Saskatchewan, he passed his country's Bill of Rights, and presided over the opening of the St. Lawrence Seaway.

question.leadin: These people may have inspired the tuniit("toon-EAT"), a race of giants in a successor culture's mythology.
question.text: Name this archaeological culture, which preceded the Thule people in northern Canada and Greenland. Bows and arrows are conspicuously absent from their sites despite their use by the previous Saqqaq ("sah-KAHK") culture.
question.clue: X-shaped incisions on figures' heads from this culture have been linked to shamanistic travels.

swap.text: The Yupik peoples and these people of the Arctic and Subarctic were direct descendants of the Thule peoples. These indigenous people identified the Dorset as giants that they call the Tuniit.
swap.answerHtml: Inuit [accept Inupiat or Iñupiaq; accept Eskimo but inform the player that the term is considered offensive]
swap.clue: In the 1950s, this ethnic group's dogs were killed by the RCMP.

question.text: This Liberal Prime Minister from 1948-57 enthusiastically got Canada on board NATO, expanded social security, and directed his Secretary of State for External Affairs, Lester Pearson, to resolve the Suez Crisis.
question.answerHtml: Louis St. Laurent [or Louis Stephen St. Laurent; or Louis-Etienne St-Laurent]
question.clue: This Canadian Prime Minister preceded John Diefenbaker. This Prime Minister helped establish NATO, while his foreign affairs minister Lester Pearson helped broker the Suez Crisis.

swap.leadin: During the Cold War, the governments of Canada and the United States historically operated this defensive line of radar stations.
swap.text: Name this line of stations at sites including Point Lay, Alaska and Alert, Nunavut. Either the three-word name or the three-letter acronym they are more commonly known by are acceptable.

question.text: The Popham settlement was a direct reaction to the St. Croix settlement of 1604, briefly capital of this French New World territory that notionally spanned the Bay of Fundy, Nova Scotia, and the Atlantic Coast of Canada.
question.clue: This colony had its southern border with colonial Maine established along the Kennebec River.

swap.leadin: This event is commemorated every December 6th with the ringing of a bell at a tower in Fort Needham Park.
swap.text: Identify this event partially involving the SS Imo, which was flying a Norwegian flag. Some people were harmed by the 60-foot high tsunami during this event.
swap.clue: One group killed in this event were sent by the Commission for Relief in Belgium, and this event destroyed the Horatio-Brannan- captained Stella Maris.
